items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1961-06-06
items.q: And I think that was the three pianists that I had. Freeman, Lloyd Glenn, oh no, Jay Golson.

ctx.x: That was later then. That is correct. Much later. That's when it was first recorded. Paul Gayton is the one that put it on. Then later on I got Camille Howard to play it but she played it in the wrong vein. She played it in the jump tempo and You Don't Love Me isn't a jump song. It was the theme song of the band. Cottrell, myself and Lloyd Glenn. The pianist that was in my band. He came after Freeman didn't he? Long after Freeman. Yes he came quite a while after Freeman. I think that, I'm not for sure I think…
You had a regular arranger for your band?

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1969-12-30
items.q: And then we had the piano player, Lloyd Glenn, came in later times after Al Freeman, who was the first piano player.

ctx.x: Okay, this is Don Albert, Real 2, December the 30th, 1969, I believe it is. Okay, I wanted to ask you about the arrangers in your band a little bit. Now, who did most of the arrangers?

Well, when the band first left here, when I organized it here in New Orleans, there weren't any arrangers. We would take the stocks and we would rearrange the stocks to fit what we wanted, and how we wanted it. But we were concentrating on our original style of playing. And the first arranger that I had in the band was a fellow out of Little Rock, Arkansas. He is still living today. His name is Philander Tiller, an alto player. Now, Phil was a tremendous arranger. And he could write arrangements that he couldn't…
Did you ever hear him talk about Cuba? Cuban Bennett?

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1972-09-18
items.q: Of course, we had Al Freeman, that great pianist.

ctx.x: Yeah. I always get the impression they were very refined fellows.

Well, a very refined group of fellows. I don't think you can find too many like they were today. Well, for instance, I went to school with Cottrell. Mm-hmm. And, we, well, he was a little bit behind me because he's a little younger than I am. Of course, we had Al Freeman, that great pianist. His son is not at the movie store, Al Freeman Jr.

items.title: Don Albert and Herbert Hall Interview, 1978-08-03
items.q: Al Freeman. Al Freeman. Where was he from? He was from New Orleans. He was from New Orleans. So the band really was New Orleans musicians at the time.

ctx.x: Yeah. And who was the first piano player?
Al Freeman. Al Freeman. Where was he from? He was from New Orleans. He was from New Orleans. So the band really was New Orleans musicians at the time. Guys that were from there, mainly. No, no, no.
